notes: Reconstruction reading basis (e.g. Streitberg Gothic sound convention, Wiktionary period-pronunciation scopes, Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese). A reconstruction is never D (CONSTITUTION 1.1); the row is routed to the sealed gold file.
Historical stage with a reviewed reading rule but no reading model: citation lemma of a documentary lect, not a spoken tip (CONSTITUTION 3.6).
Source supplies an editorial historical reading; still a lemma interpretation, not recorded speech.
Segments come from a mechanical source-side conversion of a written lemma.
Original spelling or script only; no phonetic reading is asserted.
Broad reading inferred by a reviewed orthographic profile.
IE-CoR cites normalized dictionary lemmata with expert segment conversions; for ancient stages these are documentary citation forms, never low-sigma spoken tips.
DiACL lexical entries are normalized lemmata compiled from handbooks and dictionaries.
Dyen et al. lexicostatistical list: normalized citation lemmata.
Intercontinental Dictionary Series: dictionary lemmata, often in source orthography.
Linguistic Survey of India comparative vocabulary: colonial-era normalized transcriptions.
GLED: ASJP-derived representations; normalization cannot restore omitted contrasts.
Wiktionary entry: supplied IPA or a reviewed source-specific profile; crowd-edited, not field transcription.
Fallback for unreviewed wordlist sources (lexibank-style standardized transcriptions). Marked source_class_fallback in meta.
